A browser with no HTML, no CSS, and no "web pages" in the traditional sense.

Sounds like just another AI startup making empty promises. But after a closer look, I realized this is anything but simple.

In late April 2026, a product named Flipbook.page officially launched. Its self-introduction is just one sentence:

An AI-powered infinite visual browser.

You open it, type in a question, and what you see isn't a list of links returned by a search engine, nor is it a text response from ChatGPT.

What you see is a visual scene.

A visual scene generated in real-time by AI based on your current needs. You scroll, and the scene changes. You ask follow-up questions, and the scene adapts. You turn the page, and every page is brand new—not a pre-designed template, but created for you by AI in that exact moment.

The Key Difference Isn't About Aesthetics, But Information Shifting from "Finding" to "Creating"

The logic of a traditional browser is: you enter a URL → the server returns code → the browser renders the page. The page is pre-written, and the structure everyone sees is basically identical.

Flipbook's logic is: you input a request → AI understands the intent → it generates the visual in real-time. The content and format can be different for everyone.

This isn't a difference of degree; it's two completely different ways of organizing information.

Search engines have dominated the internet for over twenty years, relying on a simple logic: there is a massive amount of information on the internet, but it's too scattered, so you need a tool to help you find it.

But what if information no longer needs to be found?

If AI can directly generate the complete content you need based on your request, where does the value of a search engine lie? Google's moat is indexing pages across the entire internet, but what if users no longer need to visit those pages?

The Team Behind It Is Quite Interesting

Behind Flipbook is a team worth watching: former engineers and designers from OpenAI, Humane, and Apple.

Let's break it down:

The OpenAI folks understand the capability boundaries of large language models and generative AI.

The Humane folks have explored hardware-plus-AI interactions. Although the Humane AI Pin wasn't much of a commercial success, the interaction design experience is very real.

The Apple folks understand the ultimate pursuit of user experience and visual design.

With these three groups coming together, they aren't building just another wrapper app. They are targeting a more fundamental question: If information no longer needs to be presented through code, what should the medium for information be?

Compared to Existing Tools, What Exactly Makes It Different?

Many people's first reaction is: isn't this just an AI chat tool with a visual interface slapped on?

Not really. Let's compare them one by one.

Compared to search engines: Google gives you links, and you need to click, navigate, read, and filter. Flipbook gives you a direct presentation of the answer, requiring no navigation or secondary processing. The search engine's job is to "find," while Flipbook's job is to "create."

Compared to ChatGPT: Conversational AI gives you text, occasionally accompanied by images or code. Flipbook gives you a complete visual experience—text, images, layout, information hierarchy—all generated in one go. Conversational AI is about Q&A; Flipbook is about presentation.

Compared to traditional browsers: This is the most fundamental difference. Traditional browsers are information porters, bringing things that already exist on the internet right in front of you. Flipbook is an information creator; every page is unprecedented.

What Does This Mean for Small and Medium Business Owners?

If this kind of thing truly takes off, several industries will be directly impacted.

Education: Textbooks are uniformly written, but a Flipbook-style experience could generate different learning materials for each student, tailored to their comprehension level, interests, and learning pace. Would the very concept of a "textbook" still exist?

E-commerce: Traditional e-commerce relies on shelf-style displays. What if AI could directly generate personalized product display pages based on your needs? No need to browse, no need to compare; AI simply tells you exactly what suits you.

Travel: Travel guides are currently just text-and-image lists. What if AI could generate a complete, visual, and interactive travel itinerary based on your preferences, budget, and schedule?

News: News is currently presented in a standardized article format. What if AI could generate different forms of news presentation based on your reading habits—some prefer timelines, some prefer comparison charts, some prefer key takeaways?

These aren't just predictions; they are directions. Which specific path proves viable and advances fastest depends on both technological development and user choice.

Several Signals Worth Observing

Flipbook is still an early-stage product. However, there are several signals worth tracking continuously.

First, user retention. It's not hard to get a first-time use driven by novelty; the hard part is whether users will come back for a second or third time. If retention metrics are good, it proves this isn't just a gimmick, but a genuine need.

Second, generation speed and cost. Real-time visual generation requires immense computing power. If costs can't be brought down or speed can't keep up, the experience will suffer.

Third, content quality and controllability. If the AI-generated visuals aren't accurate enough, aesthetically pleasing enough, or controllable enough, users will leave.

Fourth, will an ecosystem grow around it? Traditional browsers gave rise to the entire internet ecosystem. Can Flipbook cultivate a similar ecosystem? Will developers be willing to create on its platform?
